_comment: Recommended per-PLUGIN settings, offered as an apply-or-skip substep of the guided walks' plugin layer and read by scripts/plugin-settings.js; /alfred-code:init applies the claude-hud row through scripts/hud-statusline.js, after the statusLine it gates. A plugin ships its own defaults; this catalog holds only the keys THIS stack has a reason to change, each with a `why` a user can weigh. Row shape: `verified` (the exact plugin version + file the keys were read from - a key the plugin does not read is a silent no-op, so never add one from memory), `scope` (`account` when the plugin's config file is account-level whichever scope the plugin was installed at), and `targets[]` - `file` (path relative to the ACCOUNT config dir: CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, else ~/.claude), `settings` (the object to deep-merge), `why` (per top-level key group), the optional `requires_path` (dotted path that must already exist in the target, else the target is skipped - a patch to a block the plugin's own setup writes must not invent that block), the optional `chosen_by` (key -> another dotted path whose presence means the user already chose that key, so it is reported and kept), and the optional `on_platform` (a Node `process.platform` name -> leaves merged over `settings` on that platform only; each changes a value `settings` already sets, so its `why` covers it - lint 28). The script only ADDS missing keys by default: a value the user already chose is reported as a difference and kept unless they explicitly pick replace.

claude-hud.verified: claude-hud 0.15.0 - src/config.ts DEFAULT_CONFIG (key names + shipped defaults: every key below present - lineLayout, showSeparators, the eight display keys, gitStatus.showAheadBehind and showFileStats), mergeConfig and migrateLegacyLayout (a legacy layout key migrated only while lineLayout is absent), src/schema.ts DESCRIPTIONS (lineLayout `compact` is the single-line layout; showSeparators draws its rule in compact only) and its NOTES 'refresh' text (refreshInterval on the statusLine entry in settings.json; 30 s or more on Windows Git Bash with several sessions), collector.mjs claudePaths (configPath <config dir>/plugins/claude-hud/config.json); first read on 0.8.0; 0.12.0 added display.showAgentEffort (default false, not set here); 0.15.0 moved the config from dist/config.js to src/config.ts and replaced commands/setup.md and configure.md with one `hud` skill

why.lineLayout: claude-hud's own compact layout: one line under the prompt instead of the multi-line default, so the HUD costs the least terminal height in every session
why.showSeparators: the same layout without the rule compact draws between the session line and the activity lines
why.display: the stack's own working surface, on screen: skills / MCP / agents / tools are what an alfred-code session actually runs (the same four analyze-usage.js reconstructs from the transcript afterwards), config counts say whether this project's rules and hooks really loaded, cost is the number the flow-vs-single benchmarks turn on, the effort level is pinned per seat and otherwise invisible after a runtime /effort, and the prompt-cache expiry decides whether a pause costs a full re-read
why.gitStatus: the git preferences' anti-split discipline: unpushed commits and the working-tree file counts are the two things the pre-commit checkpoint asks about

why.statusLine: Claude Code re-runs the statusline only on events (a message, /compact, a mode change, a rate-limit reset, a prompt-cache expiry), so every time-based field (usage reset countdown, session duration) freezes while a session is idle; claude-hud 0.15.0's own refresh note (src/schema.ts NOTES, 'refresh') asks for a refreshInterval to keep them ticking - 5 s, the interval 0.8.0 suggested, and 30 s on Windows (on_platform win32), where the same note says short intervals with several sessions open fail under Git Bash ('add_item ... failed, errno 1') and to 'use 30 s or more'
